findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed members of staff to be missing food handlers training. Discussed with PIC, remaining staff will complete training. Ensure any food handling staff members have completed the food handlers training within 30 days of employment. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Multiple cans with significant dents are observed on the rack in the dry storage room as ready for use. The PIC was shown and moved the cans to the separate shelf designated for dented cans. Ensure that dented cans are separated from cans intended for use to prevent a possible botulism infection in the facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: Inspector observed an employee move from loading soiled silverware into a dish rack to moving a tray of clean cups from the clean dish side and take a piece of parchment paper to lay over the cups in order to cover them. The employee was stopped and the parchment discarded. The employee was coached on maintaining hands (even gloved hands) clean when moving between soiled and clean dishes. The violation is considered corrected on site. Employee was observed properly washing hands during the remainder of the inspection.   

FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Inspector observed plastic cups heavily soiled with some sort of build up that looks like lime. The cups shall be properly cleaned and sanitized before their next use. Maintain cups and other plastic ware clean to sight and touch. The cups are heavily laden with residue so that clear cups appear to be white in color. The dish machine has a dispenser for rinse aid but there is none attached to the machine. Manager stated that they are not given the rinse aid to use with the machine.

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

(C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed two large rolls of ground beef to be thawing in a large basin of cold water. Meat was not thawing submerged under running water (water temp 70F or below). Discussed with employee. Inspector asked employee to continue thawing under running water. COS. Ensure staff is aware of appropriate thawing methods.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. 

Observed several sticky glue pads under the dish machine/3 compartment sink area to have a large amount of dead juvenile roaches. Discussed frequent changes of sticky pads with PIC. Several dead roaches around the sticky pads as well. Facility has a historic issue with roaches and it has been addressing in past inspections. See staff changes sticky pads as needed to rid facility of dead pests. Sweep as needed under this area or any other area where dead roaches are present - wash, rinse, sanitize. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed the reach-in cooler shelving to be rusting. Seal and/or repaint the shelving. Predominately in the second reach-in cooler near the reach-in freezer. Discussed with PIC. Non-food contact surfaces should smooth and easily cleanable. Rust is chipping paint away from the shelving. Repair by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of replacement or cleaning:
1. Floor fan (to circulate air) near the reach-in freezer and second reach-in cooler has accumulation of dust. Clean fan.
2. Metal baking trays stored under the main prep table shelf and below the steam table need replaced. Heavy amount of caked on, black food debris on trays. Replace trays as needed before next routine inspection. Discard old baking trays. Debris cannot be washed, rinsed, and sanitized to remove.
3. Interior of dish machine has hard water on the sides of the doors and ceiling. Utilize de-liner to reduce hard water debris. 

Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned and/or replaced before next routine inspection. These are repeat violations inches the last routine inspection on 6/27/22.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no certified food protection manager upon beginning of inspection. PIC stated that CFPM was off today and he was alone in the kitchen today - only a food handler’s license. Employee was engaged in food manipulation behaviors without a CFPM present. Discussed with Manager and PIC that a CFPM should be present during all hours of operation. Ensure another employee takes the licensure class and a copy of certification is available at the facility. Facility should have at least 2 certified food protection managers.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed a number of gnats in the kitchen, predominantly by the back door and the hand sink. Discussed gnat controls with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 7/7/22.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed plates near hot holding to be right-side up. Facility historically has an issue with this practice. Flip plates over so food- and lip-contact surfaces are not exposed to cross contamination. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff is aware of correct practices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas to be in need of replacement or cleaning:
1. Serving trays are chipped on edges. Replace trays. This is a repeat violation since the pre-opening on 5/9/22.
2. Fans within the reach-in cooler (interior ceiling) have accumulation of dust. Clean fans.
3. Floor fan (to circulate air) near the reach-in freezer and second reach-in cooler has accumulation of dust. Clean fan.
4. Metal baking trays stored under the main prep table shelf in the middle of the kitchen need replaced. Heavy amount of caked on, black food debris on trays. Replace trays before next routine inspection. Debris cannot be washed, rinsed, and sanitized to remove.
5. Interior of dish machine has hard water on the side of the doors and ceiling. Utilized de-limer to reduce hard water debris. 

Ensure nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned or replaced before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the main prep table legs and arms to have paint chipping away from the metal. Repaint this prep table. Shelf below and top prep surface itself are stainless steel and are not in need of repairs. Repair before next routine inspection.

Observed holes in the ceiling where fluorescent lighting use to be. Manager stated the area is going to repaired. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection. Area should be smooth and easily cleanable. Area is in front of reach-in freezer.
